newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares fall, trading still delayed by system.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares fall, trading still delayed by system.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped on Tuesday for the second day running in sluggish trading slowed even more by a new computerised trading system, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index fell 0.55 points to 233.74 points in lower than average turnover of 35.63 million ($10.48 million).
"The market is very healthy but we're going through a stage where there is a transition to another more efficient system," said Ali el-Tahri, a senior partner at brokers Hermes-EFG.
"There are delays, volumes are lower than usual, but these growing pains are perfectly normal."

Drugs firms Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries and Memphis Pharmaceuticals and Chemical Industries were among the day's most active stocks, but both firms ended unchanged at 158.00 pounds and 61.00.
Investors were also interested in Nile Pharmaceuticals and the stock rose 0.50 to 51.50.

The popular milling sector was also in the limelight but ended mostly down. Recent listings Upper Egypt Flour Mills rose 1.82 to 46.82 but others, led by North Cairo Flour Mills which fell 1.00 to 112.00, ended lower.

Despite the recent slippage, Tahri said the market was still attractive and that Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak's decision to hold a Middle East economic summit in November as planned was helping maintain investor confidence.

"The conference shows that Egypt is committed to economic growth and that's extremely important. Today's announcement is an important step in maintaining that ever increasing confidence in the market," he said.
Egypt had said it would link holding the conference to Israeli progress on peace negotiations with the Palestinians.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 360.62 points from 364.86 on Monday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 161.93 points from 161.41.
